context.note: Items marked merged are in the master branch only. They are not in a release until a release containing them is published.

status_scale.discussion: talked about on a list or forum, no concrete proposal
status_scale.proposal: written proposal (BIP draft, design doc, PR description) not yet merged
status_scale.merged: merged into a project's main branch, not yet released
status_scale.released: shipped in a tagged release of that software
status_scale.documentation: specification or documentation change only; no software behavior changes

items.title: Peers are no longer disconnected for a missed ping while they are sending us blocks
items.what_happened: Bitcoin Core stops enforcing the 20-minute ping timeout against a peer while blocks are being downloaded from that peer.
items.why_it_matters: During initial block download on a slow link, a peer busy serving our block requests could miss the ping deadline and be dropped although it was not at fault. This avoids needless disconnects for low-bandwidth nodes.
items.not_yet: In master only; not in a release. No consensus or policy change.

items.title: Private transaction broadcast now always completes all three initial connections
items.what_happened: When a node initiates a private broadcast of a transaction, it now completes all three initial broadcast connections instead of stopping early when the transaction comes back or conflicts.
items.why_it_matters: Stopping early could leak timing information that helps link a transaction to its origin. The PR addresses theoretical timing attacks raised in earlier review of the private-broadcast work.
affects: users who broadcast transactions privately through Bitcoin Core
items.not_yet: In master only; not in a release. Check release notes for when private broadcast and this fix ship.
items.uncertainty: The attacks addressed are described as theoretical in the PR.

items.title: Wallets record which client version last opened and decrypted them
items.what_happened: The wallet now records the version of the last Bitcoin Core client that opened it and that decrypted it.
items.why_it_matters: Groundwork for future automatic wallet upgrades: if a wallet is upgraded, opened in an older version, then opened in a newer one again, the newer client can detect this and redo the upgrade instead of leaving mixed upgraded and non-upgraded data.
affects: wallet users who switch between Bitcoin Core versions
items.not_yet: In master only; not in a release. No new automatic upgrade ships with this change; it prepares for later ones.

items.title: PSBT type registry adds the missing PSBT_IN_P2C_TWEAK (0x19) entry
items.what_happened: The BIP-174 PSBT field registry now lists input key type 0x19, PSBT_IN_P2C_TWEAK, defined in BIP-372 (pay-to-contract tweak fields). It had been left out when the tables moved into the registry.
items.why_it_matters: The registry exists so new BIPs do not reuse a key type that is already taken. A missing row risks a collision in a future proposal.
items.not_yet: Documentation fix only; no change to consensus, node software or existing PSBT behavior.

items.title: Large socket timeouts no longer break bitcoin-cli connections on macOS
items.what_happened: Socket waits cap each timeout at INT_MAX milliseconds, avoiding macOS select() errors for bitcoin-cli -rpcclienttimeout=0 and other very large values.
items.why_it_matters: The documented no-timeout setting could instead fail to connect on macOS. The shared cap also avoids integer narrowing in poll() on Linux.
items.not_yet: In master only; not in a release. A requested 32.x backport is not evidence of a shipped fix.

items.title: Silent Payments extraction rejects misleading P2PKH scriptSig public keys
items.what_happened: Bitcoin Core finds the compressed public-key push whose HASH160 matches the spent P2PKH output, rather than evaluating scriptSig with a dummy signature checker.
items.why_it_matters: A third party could modify scriptSig so the dummy checker selected the wrong public key. Correct extraction is necessary for Silent Payments processing.
items.not_yet: In master only; not in a release. This does not establish release availability of Silent Payments or change consensus.
items.uncertainty: The author reports existing Silent Payments implementations appeared unaffected; this is not evidence of deployed wallet losses.

items.title: LND checks blinded-path fee arithmetic instead of wrapping uint32 totals
items.what_happened: Blinded-path fee aggregation uses checked uint64 arithmetic and rejects totals that cannot fit invoice payinfo fields. An invalid candidate route is skipped without discarding other usable routes.
items.why_it_matters: Overflow could advertise fees below the actual forwarding policy, leading to underpayment and failure after the multipart-payment timeout. The report traces the issue to blinded receiving introduced in v0.18.3.
items.not_yet: In master only; not in a release. This is an LND implementation fix, not a Lightning protocol change.

items.title: LND fixes address aliasing and short reads in NodeAnnouncement2
items.what_happened: NodeAnnouncement2 decoding stops sharing address backing storage across loop iterations and reads fixed-width address fields completely, rejecting truncated records.
items.why_it_matters: Multiple addresses could collapse onto the last decoded address, and incomplete IPv4, IPv6 or Tor v3 records could be accepted with zero-filled bytes.
items.not_yet: In master only; not in a release. No wire-format change is implied.
items.uncertainty: The linked issue reports parser correctness failures, not a confirmed live exploit or network-wide gossip impact.

items.title: Core Lightning v26.06.9 ships security fixes and repairs gossip throttling
items.what_happened: Core Lightning released v26.06.9 with security fixes across channel and message handling, rune authorization and configuration. It fixes the v26.06.8 gossip-throttle regression and adds reproducible ARM binaries.
items.why_it_matters: Maintainers strongly recommend upgrading. Ordinary gossip, pings and onion messages no longer consume the gossip-query throttle budget; restricted runes cannot bypass restrictions through the documented creation and relisting paths.
items.not_yet: Released for Core Lightning only; not a Bitcoin consensus activation. Dual funding remains experimental, and newer master database schemas cannot downgrade to 26.06.x.
items.uncertainty: Security regression tests are temporarily withheld by maintainers; release notes do not provide complete exploit details.

items.title: LND backports BOLT 2 fee-state handling to 0.20.x and 0.21.x
items.what_happened: The fee-state fix already merged into master in August was backported to v0.20.x-branch and v0.21.x-branch. Unobserved fee updates replace the previous value; mailbox admission has message-count and serialized-size limits.
items.why_it_matters: This aligns in-memory fee updates with BOLT 2 replacement semantics and bounds queued channel messages. Admission failures reconnect rather than silently dropping ordered messages.
items.not_yet: The merged status refers to upstream master PR #11023, not the maintenance branches. These backports are not in a release verified by this review; branch merges alone do not establish availability.
items.uncertainty: Upstream merged on August 7, outside this window; the new events are the October 8 backports. No tagged release containing these backports was established.
